thread:
maya: Quick experiment summary from yesterday's run on staging-gpu-3 — adaptive buffer-swap scheduler + kernel-hinting prototype. Leaving raw numbers here before I file an RFC.

maya: TL;DR: under mixed small/long-chat workload with 3 models co-resident we saw allocator pressure down (alloc latency -18%), swap count -42%, token throughput +6% for short sequences, but p99 tail for seq>2048 rose ~2.1% due to a kernel-fallback memcpy hot-path.

maya: Key changes: weighted-LRU swap prioritizer (prefers older model-owned KV unless recent reuse observed), speculative prefetch for predicted next-KV page, and kernel hinting that selects an alternate attention kernel when seq distribution heavy on <128 or >1536.

thomas: can you paste the scheduler config and the CLI used for profiling?

maya: sure — profiler command we used:
```
perf record -F 99 -g -- ./inference-server --model-set multi-cohost-staging.yaml --trace=alloc,swap,kernel_choice
```
and the scheduler snippet:
```json
{"swap_policy":"weighted_lru","prefetch_pct":0.3,"kernel_hinting":true,"hint_thresholds":{"short":128,"long":1536},"reuse_window_ms":5000}
```

sanjay: nice. quick q: where did prefetch fetch from — NVMe or remote object store? and did we see NVMe bandwidth saturation?

maya: prefetch reads hot pages from local NVMe (we stage most model shards there). Observed NVMe peak ~420 MB/s (disk capable 1.1 GB/s). So not saturated. Swap IO total reduced ~47% vs baseline. Prefetch avoided ~1.2k swap reads during 10m steady-state.

elaine: how deterministic is the weighted-LRU scoring? i.e., any oscillation between models when they have similar recency?

maya: we bias by a small hysteresis term + reuse_count; scoring = age_seconds * (1 + 0.2*reuse_count) to avoid flip-flop. Tested with synthetic traffic and no oscillation for 30m.

rachel: what about the p99 uptick — is that the kernel hinting or the prefetch interaction?

maya: digging in flamegraphs — p99 increase correlated with kernel fallback path taken when sequence >1536 but kernel selection missed early because initial length estimate was low (we estimate from first token batch). Fallback path does memcpy + re-alloc workspace: extra ~2.4ms on p99.

thomas: can we avoid fallback by precomputing a small fast heuristic at accept time? e.g., look at delta between first and second batch lengths or look at user-specified max_seq param?

maya: yes — planned change: check request.metadata.max_length if present, else sample first 8 tokens to estimate. If predicted longer than threshold, pick long-seq kernel up-front. Patch prototype:
```diff
- choose_kernel(estimated_len)
+ choose_kernel(estimated_len, user_max)
+   if user_max && user_max > 1400: pick_long_kernel()
+   else if sample_predicts_long(): pick_long_kernel()
```

sanjay: also consider making fallback path elide full memcpy by keeping a tiny standby workspace page mapped to avoid re-allocation. saves memcopy but small memory overhead.

maya: good call — I added a spare 4 MB standby workspace per worker in another run; memcopy count dropped 88% and p99 tail recovered. Standby page cost ~0.1% VRAM.

elaine: any implications for multi-model co-residency? i.e., standby pages per worker might inflate resident set and reduce packable models per GPU.

maya: measured that too: with 8 workers standby pages increased resident VRAM by ~0.8 GB total, reducing packable tiny models by 1 on a 48 GB card. But tradeoff seems acceptable for stable p99. We can gate standby pages based on density signals.

rachel: can we do density-aware standby: e.g., only enable standby when pack_density < 0.9?

maya: yep that's next RFC item. I sketched a config:
```json
{"standby_policy":"density_aware","density_threshold":0.9}
```

thomas: aside: did kernel hinting change our kernel cache hit rate? any JIT churn?

maya: kernel cache hit rate improved for short sequences because we avoided fallback-induced kernel switch. Overall kernel JIT churn negligible in staging. We did see one regression in warmup-time: cataloging new kernel variants added ~120ms to cold-start of a worker; mitigated by prewarming in dedicated pool.

ops-bot: deploy/ci passed for branch refs/heads/adaptive-swap-scheduler (build 4872) :white_check_mark:

maya: next steps: I will open RFC with data and proposal to default-enable kernel-upfront heuristic + optional standby workspace with density gate. Planning rollout to canary running 10% of mixed-cohost workloads next week.

thomas: SGTM. please add perf dashboards (alloc latency, swap count, kernel-fallback-rate, p99 by seq-bucket).

maya: will do. tagging @rachel for console dashboard layout input. :spiral_notepad:

rachel: got it — will prototype few panels.
